title: Making a Case: Argumentative Essays
text:
An argumentative essay is a form of writing in which the author takes a clear position on a debatable issue and tries to persuade the reader to accept it. Unlike a simple description, it must rely on evidence, such as statistics, expert opinions, or real examples. A strong essay also acknowledges the counterarguments, because readers are more likely to trust a writer who considers opposing views fairly. Finally, the writer organises the ideas so that each paragraph supports the central thesis.

Many students find this type of writing difficult at first because they confuse expressing an opinion with presenting an argument. A good opinion is not enough; the writer must explain why the opinion is reasonable. For this reason, teachers often recommend that learners plan their essays before writing, listing the main reasons and the evidence for each one. With regular practice, the structure becomes more natural, and the argument becomes more convincing.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must an argumentative essay rely on?
options: Evidence such as statistics and expert opinions

questions.text: What do teachers often recommend, according to the second paragraph?
options: Writing the essay without any planning
Avoiding the use of evidence altogether
Planning the essay and listing reasons and evidence before writing

questions.text: Why does a strong essay acknowledge the counterarguments?
options: Because it can make the writer's own position seem more credible
Because the writer should agree with the opposing side
Because it makes the essay shorter and easier to read
Because counterarguments are usually proven to be true

questions.text: What is the main difficulty for students described in the second paragraph?
options: They do not have access to a computer
They dislike reading articles about current issues
They confuse giving an opinion with building a reasoned argument
They never receive feedback from their teachers

vocabulary.definition: to make someone agree with a belief or accept an idea
facts or information that support a claim
arguments that oppose a main argument
the central claim that a piece of writing defends

paragraph_translations: Um ensaio argumentativo é uma forma de escrita em que o autor assume uma posição clara sobre uma questão discutível e tenta convencer o leitor a aceitá-la. Ao contrário de uma simples descrição, ele deve apoiar-se em evidências, como estatísticas, opiniões de especialistas ou exemplos reais. Um ensaio forte também reconhece os contra-argumentos, porque os leitores tendem a confiar mais em um escritor que considera com justiça os pontos de vista opostos. Por fim, o escritor organiza as ideias para que cada parágrafo sustente a tese central.

Muitos estudantes acham esse tipo de escrita difícil no início, porque confundem expressar uma opinião com apresentar um argumento. Uma boa opinião não é suficiente; o escritor precisa explicar por que a opinião é razoável. Por isso, os professores costumam recomendar que os alunos planejem seus ensaios antes de escrever, listando as principais razões e as evidências de cada uma. Com a prática regular, a estrutura torna-se mais natural e o argumento torna-se mais convincente.
